q: An antagonist that directly neutralizes an agonist, such as a chelator binding a heavy metal, is exerting:
w: Chemical antagonism is direct neutralization of the agonist, as when a chelator binds a metal. It needs no receptor, unlike physiologic (separate receptor, opposite effect) or pharmacologic (same receptor) antagonism.
k: Direct neutralization of the agonist = chemical antagonism.

q: When two drugs act at DIFFERENT receptors to produce opposite physiologic effects, the interaction is called:
w: Physiologic (functional) antagonism uses two separate receptors that drive opposite effects, so the net response is blunted. Pharmacologic antagonism instead blocks the same receptor the agonist uses.
k: Opposite effects via different receptors = physiologic antagonism.
